title: Approval, rule-package and case-move operation names are not published
source: Architecture v5 slides 13-14 and 19; TSD S6 T5.2 and Appendix T-A; context pack ownership rows
description: The committee approval act is named as one decide operation on the architecture slides and carried as approve, return and refuse rows in the ownership rows, while no source publishes a name for the DS rule-package read or for the case-move answer a stage sends to rwb-case. Nothing says which of the two forms is the contract of record. The contract and the APP story bind to the published documents and carry the section R9 placeholder for the three names until the owners publish them.
evidence: Slide 14 gives POST /approvals/{id}/decide; the ownership rows give three act rows; TSD S6 T5.2 names P3, P7 and P4 interfaces without operation names
proposed: rwb-decision and rwb-case publish the operation names and the act form; the contract is re-tagged and the placeholders removed.

title: Plan contract-dependency row is empty while five cross-service contracts are consumed
source: split_plan.json slices RWB-S6-E6001-APP and RWB-S6-E6001-CON; TSD S6 T5.2
description: Both slices carry an empty C row, yet the approval slice consumes five cross-service contracts: the rwb-decision approval chain, the rwb-decision rule package, the rwb-access DoA limit, the rwb-case state read and the rwb-case move answer. Under R5.4 a C dependency never blocks the build, so the omission changes the dependency map rather than the plan of work, and the story is built against the published documents and fakes on Day 1.
evidence: split_plan.json C rows for RWB-S6-E6001-APP and RWB-S6-E6001-CON are empty; the story sections 12.2 list five consumed rows
proposed: The dependency map adds the five C rows when the fragments are assembled; the build order does not change.

title: No event is published in this key although the service owns EV-23
source: TSD S6 T5.3; context pack ownership rows; legacy story RWB-E6-001 Endpoints table
description: The service owns one event, EV-23 LotAwarded, first in E6, and the legacy story lists only two endpoints and no event. No source states whether the committee approval publishes a fact of its own. The contract declares EV-23 as the award story's event and no event in this key, so the approval leaves the service on the case-move answer and on the read.
evidence: Context pack events row: EV-23, one event; TSD S6 T5.3 lists LotAwarded as published; the legacy story has no event row
proposed: If the approval must publish, EV-23 is split into an approval fact and an award fact by the event catalogue owner.

title: Committee approver has no row in the service RBAC matrix and no published DoA row
source: FSD S6 A2.5.3.3; TSD S6 T6.1
description: The FSD names Credit approval committee member as a role that also uses the feature, while the TSD RBAC matrix has no row for it and no source publishes a delegation-limit row for that role. The rights of the build are therefore the T6.1 staff and partner rows, and the committee's act is read as an approval-chain answer taken under the P4 DoA limit rather than as a Workbench role.
evidence: FSD S6 A2.5.3.3 lists Head of Asset Liquidity, Debt sale officer and Credit approval committee member; TSD S6 T6.1 has no committee row
proposed: rwb-access publishes the committee level and its delegation limits; the approval chain then names the authority this story writes.
